title: Passive but accessible:  Studied information is not actively stored in working memory, yet attended regardless of anticipated load
description: This EEG dataset investigates how attended information is maintained in working memory despite varying cognitive load expectations. Participants performed a color-recall task with two memory screens presenting studied and novel objects under conditions of high or low anticipated load. The study examines neural correlates of working memory maintenance and the effects of load expectation on memory-related brain activity, using event-related potentials and spectral analysis of EEG signals.
methods_description: EEG was recorded during a working memory task involving two memory screens (1000 ms each) separated by a 1400 ms interstimulus interval. Participants memorized objects on the first screen and performed color-recall responses on a continuous color wheel. Load expectation was manipulated by varying the probability of additional items appearing on the second screen (80% in high-load condition, 20% in low-load condition). Corrective feedback was provided for studied objects with errors exceeding 40°.
